selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Batch 35

profiles.name: Chester Clute
profiles.excerpt: Chester Clute carried a prolific Hollywood character career into Lux Radio Theatre, where his sharply defined supporting style translated naturally to the microphone.
profiles.bio_html:
Chester Clute was born in Orange, New Jersey in 1891 and built a long career as a stage and film character actor. Broadway preceded a Hollywood career of roughly 250 films, where he became especially familiar in brief, sharply etched comic and supporting roles.

Lux Radio Theatre made use of the same character technique. Clute's screen experience allowed him to establish small parts quickly around featured stars without drawing attention away from the central performance.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 10 Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Clute, documenting the radio side of a career better known from film.

profiles.name: Eda Reiss Merin
profiles.excerpt: Eda Reiss Merin was a six-decade stage, radio, film and television actress who also helped build the professional institutions that supported broadcast performers.
profiles.bio_html:
Eda Reiss Merin was born in New York City in 1913 and entered professional theatre while still young. She worked with major stage companies, appeared on Broadway and developed a career that eventually stretched across more than six decades.

Radio was a substantial part of Merin's professional life, and she was also an early organizer of AFTRA. Her later work ranged from regional theatre and television to film and voice acting, including the Disney feature The Black Cauldron.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three NBC University Theater performances credited to Merin and additional appearances on Broadway Is My Beat, Escape, Rocky Fortune, The Adventures of Philip Marlowe and The Line Up.

profiles.name: Elaine Rost
profiles.excerpt: Elaine Rost was a New York radio repertory actress whose surviving work crosses crime, psychological drama and science fiction.
profiles.bio_html:
Elaine Rost belongs to the professional New York radio repertory of the 1950s, where actors moved constantly among anthology, crime and speculative drama. Personal biographical documentation is limited, so her profile remains anchored to verified broadcasts.

Rost appeared on CBS Radio Workshop, Crime and Peter Chambers, The Chase, X Minus One, Dimension X and Rocky Fortune. That range shows a performer trusted in both realistic crime stories and more experimental material.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves two performances each on CBS Radio Workshop, Crime and Peter Chambers, The Chase and X Minus One credited to Rost, plus appearances on Dimension X and Rocky Fortune.

profiles.name: Grey Stafford
profiles.excerpt: Grey Stafford was a supporting radio actor whose surviving GRH work is concentrated in NBC University Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Grey Stafford is best documented through the postwar radio repertory, especially the literary adaptations of NBC University Theater. Personal biographical detail is limited, so the surviving broadcast record provides the strongest basis for his profile.

Stafford also appeared in mystery drama, including The New Adventures of Nero Wolfe and The Whistler. Those credits place him across formal literary adaptation and popular suspense.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight NBC University Theater performances credited to Stafford and one appearance each on The New Adventures of Nero Wolfe and The Whistler.

profiles.name: Gwen Delano
profiles.excerpt: Gwen Delano was a West Coast radio actress whose surviving work ranges from Dragnet and Roy Rogers to Lux Radio Theatre.
profiles.bio_html:
Gwen Delano worked in the professional West Coast radio repertory during the postwar network years. Her surviving credits show a supporting actress able to move among police drama, westerns and Hollywood anthology productions.

Delano appeared on Dragnet, Lux Radio Theatre, Roy Rogers, NBC University Theater and Screen Directors Playhouse. The programs required very different performance styles, from the restrained naturalism of Dragnet to broader western and feature-film adaptation.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three performances each on Dragnet and Lux Radio Theatre credited to Delano, two Roy Rogers appearances and additional anthology work.

profiles.name: Jack Lewis
profiles.excerpt: Jack Lewis was a West Coast radio supporting actor whose surviving work is divided between Lux Radio Theatre and Pat Novak, for Hire.
profiles.bio_html:
Jack Lewis is best documented through the West Coast radio repertory. Because the name is shared by several entertainment professionals, this profile stays with the verified broadcast record rather than assigning uncertain personal history.

Lewis appeared in both Lux Radio Theatre and Pat Novak, for Hire, moving between polished Hollywood adaptation and the hard-boiled San Francisco atmosphere of Jack Webb's detective series.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five Lux Radio Theatre performances and five Pat Novak, for Hire appearances credited to Lewis.

profiles.name: Jonathan Hole
profiles.excerpt: Jonathan Hole carried a career from vaudeville and stage into radio announcing, serial drama, film and hundreds of television appearances.
profiles.bio_html:
Jonathan Hole was born in Eldora, Iowa in 1904 and began his career in vaudeville before spending years in stage and stock companies. Radio became a major professional bridge as he worked in Iowa, New York, Detroit, Chicago and Los Angeles.

Hole acted in radio serials including Ma Perkins and also worked professionally as an announcer at WBBM in Chicago. He later became a prolific film and television character actor, often playing clerks, managers and minor officials.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Hole, two Barrie Craig appearances and additional work on Columbia Workshop, Gunsmoke, Let George Do It and The Railroad Hour.

profiles.name: Kim Hunter
profiles.excerpt: Kim Hunter brought an Academy Award-winning stage and screen career into the repertory of CBS Radio Mystery Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Kim Hunter was born Janet Cole in Detroit in 1922 and trained at the Actors Studio after beginning professionally on stage and screen. Her performance as Stella Kowalski in A Streetcar Named Desire earned both an Academy Award and a Golden Globe.

Hunter continued working across theatre, film and television while returning regularly to dramatic audio. During the 1970s she became one of the recognizable repertory voices of CBS Radio Mystery Theater, appearing in mystery, suspense and supernatural stories.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 10 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Hunter, documenting a substantial radio chapter within her larger acting career.

profiles.name: Kurt Martell
profiles.excerpt: Kurt Martell was a West Coast radio repertory actor whose surviving work crosses adventure, musical anthology and crime drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Kurt Martell belongs to the working West Coast radio repertory whose surviving broadcasts provide a clearer professional record than later biographical accounts.

Martell appeared repeatedly on Escape and The Railroad Hour, with additional work on Crime Classics, Pat Novak, for Hire and The Halls of Ivy. Those assignments ranged from tense adventure to musical and domestic programming.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four Escape performances credited to Martell, three The Railroad Hour appearances and one broadcast each on Crime Classics, Pat Novak, for Hire and The Halls of Ivy.

profiles.name: Lotte Stavisky
profiles.excerpt: Lotte Stavisky was a New York radio actress whose surviving work is especially strong in the intimate supernatural drama of Quiet Please.
profiles.bio_html:
Lotte Stavisky worked in the New York radio repertory during the 1940s and 1950s. Personal biographical documentation is limited, but her broadcast credits place her repeatedly in demanding dramatic anthology.

Stavisky became especially associated with Quiet, Please, Wyllis Cooper's atmospheric series built around close microphone acting and psychological storytelling. She also appeared on Cloak and Dagger, The Adventures of the Abbotts and Words at War.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Quiet, Please performances credited to Stavisky and one appearance each on Cloak and Dagger, The Adventures of the Abbotts and Words at War.
